main_text.head: CAP. XVIII.

head.i: Undecimum nostrum Argumentum adversus Meritum de Condigno, tanquam ex Meritis Christi, ex parte Martyrii, ut est nobilissimum medium perveniendi ad vitam aternam.

main_text.head: Argumentatio.
SECT. I.
main_text.p: QUicquid excellentiæ competit omni operi bono, id utique Martyrio est tribuendum: At hoc excellentiæ, viz. De Condigno Meritorum esse vitæ æter-na, non est tribuendum Martyrio: Propterea, De Condigno Meritorum esse vitæ æternæ, non competit omni operi bono.

Major ex Scripturis facilè evincitur, in quibus Martyrium, tanquam nobilissimum medium perveniendi ad vitam æternam, sæpe anteponitur cæteris omnibus: Cui etiam Adversarios nostros assensuros esse nullùs dubito.

page.notes: The initial Q is a woodcut ornament; the word is Uicquid in print, read here as Quicquid. The catchword "I. Thæ-" has its small capitals rendered as "Thæ-" and is doubtful: [?] would apply to the letters THÆ read from the small caps. Show-through and the neighbouring page at the right edge are excluded. The page is a scan of an old book, so the ink is faint in places; no word in the body is uncertain.
